subject: Billing unit reconciliation and sample invoice for BrightCart pilot
messages:
From: Alice Zhao <alice.zhao@brightcart.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 19 May 2025 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Invoice question — rounding variance on May run

Hi Rafael,

Hope you’re well. We just pulled the May invoice for our pilot and noticed a line that shows a ~3.2% delta compared to the usage report your API console gave us. The invoice shows the per-call charges being rounded up differently than our expected token math.

Specifically: our daily usage file shows 1,246,872 tokens processed; the invoice charged 1,253,000 units (and the line-item unit is what we don’t recognize). Can you help reconcile the delta and explain how minimums/rounding were applied?

We’re trying to finalize forecasting for June and need to understand whether this is a systemic rounding rule, a context-length amortization, or something else. If helpful, I can share the internal usage CSV.

Thanks — Alice
Alice Zhao
BrightCart — Finance (Billing)
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.com>
To: Alice Zhao <alice.zhao@brightcart.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 19 May 2025 10:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Invoice question — rounding variance on May run

Hi Alice — thanks for the heads-up and the example numbers. I pulled your account’s invoice and the API usage file and attached a short sample invoice and an XLS with the line-by-line math (attachments: BrightCart_Sample_Invoice_050925.pdf, billing_calcs_brightcart_0509.xlsx). High-level explanation below; see tab "walkthrough" in the spreadsheet for the step-by-step reconciliation.

Short answer: the ~3.2% delta is explained by three factors combined — tokenization boundary rounding, per-request minimum unit application, and context-amortized packaging for long-history threads. We do not double-charge, but several rounding policies aggregate at invoice line granularity which can cause small deltas versus raw token dumps.

Key points:
- Tokenization & unitization: we bill in "billing units" mapped to 4-token quanta for this SKU. That means we round up each request’s token count to the next 4-token boundary before summing.
- Per-call minimum: for streaming/short calls we apply a 24-unit (96-token) floor per request. Only requests that are strictly above the floor are billed at their rounded unit count; sub-floor requests are billed at the floor.
- Context amortization: long conversation history is eligible for context amortization (we amortize the cost of prefix tokens across subsequent calls within a 30-minute active window). However, if a request switches model or session id, the remaining prefix is billed as a one-time re-ingest in the bill month.

In your case: the usage CSV you shared (1,246,872 raw tokens) contains ~12k short calls that each hit the 24-unit floor; after unitization and floors the summed billed units increase to 1,253,000. The attached spreadsheet shows the math:
- raw token sum -> tokenized into 4-token units per request -> apply per-call floor -> sum -> invoice-level slab rounding to nearest 10 units for line aggregation.

We also show two alternative reconstructions in the sheet ("pilot-exempt" and "no-floor") so you can see the delta by rule.

If you’d like, we can:
1) provide a line-by-line exported CSV that mirrors the invoice (useful for your GL import)
2) run one-off adjustments for the pilot month while we tidy up the export formatting

Next steps: I can prepare the line-by-line CSV and Ben/Vanessa can advise on concession/credit options. Would you prefer a one-off adjustment on May or a credit to apply against June?

Thanks,
Rafael Mendes
Head of Sales Engineering — Redwood Inference
(attachment: BrightCart_Sample_Invoice_050925.pdf; billing_calcs_brightcart_0509.xlsx)
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 19 May 2025 11:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Internal: BrightCart rounding — recommended concession options

Vanessa / Ben — quick internal note summarizing the above and proposed options to keep BrightCart during expansion. I copied the short explainer I sent Alice for context.

Summary of impact: ~3.2% net delta on May invoice (~$4.9k on their current tier). Driver: many short-event requests hitting the 24-unit floor + 4-token unitization.

Options (pick one):
A) One-off invoice adjustment — credit the delta for May and send corrected invoice.
B) Apply a promotional adjustment for the pilot (3% blanket credit for May) and offer to re-evaluate after next month once they switch to the batched SDK.
C) Leave invoice as-is but include an engineering export that fully maps line-by-line and an invoice CSV to make their GL match our billed units.

Recommended: Option B for speed (preserves revenue, simple to implement as accounting credit), but offer Option A if procurement insists on exact match for PO recs. Also recommend product helping them enable batching + prefix caching to remove the short-call floor in June.

If we do B: target credit amount $4,900, add a note on the invoice describing the pilot credit and that going forward we’ll reflect batched usage to reduce floor hits. If they want A, finance will need invoice reissue and updated tax/GL lines — longer runway.

Ben — can you prepare language for procurement/contract amendment if they request an invoice reissue? Vanessa — if we offer the discount, I’ll coordinate with finance to create the credit memo and let you draft the customer-facing note.

Rafael
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>
To: Alice Zhao <alice.zhao@brightcart.com>
Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 19 May 2025 12:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Invoice question — rounding variance on May run

Hi Alice — thanks for raising this and thanks Rafael for the clear breakdown. Quoting Rafael’s note above: 

"the ~3.2% delta is explained by three factors combined — tokenization boundary rounding, per-request minimum unit application, and context-amortized packaging for long-history threads."

We want to make this smooth for BrightCart — proposal below:
1) Apply a pilot credit equal to the delta ($4,900) to the May invoice and include a note on the June invoice describing the credit.
2) We’ll provide the line-by-line CSV export that matches the invoice so your GL team can reconcile cleanly.
3) Technical suggestion: our SDK team will share a short batching guide to reduce per-request floors; we can schedule a 30-minute call next week to walk BrightCart’s engineering through batching and prefix caching.

If you’re good with the credit, please confirm and we’ll issue the credit memo and update the June invoice. If procurement needs a reissued May invoice (no credit memo), let us know and we’ll route to finance but that typically takes 3–5 business days.

Next steps: Confirm preference (credit memo vs reissue) and whether you want the technical batching call. Happy to coordinate timing.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Account Executive — Redwood Inference
(attachment: BrightCart_Sample_Invoice_050925.pdf referenced)
